one_star_reviews.text:
I can document every interaction I'm talking about in this review with emails.  I'll use the pronouns she/her moving forward since I only ever had contact with the lady who according to Quebec's Entreprise Register (where it also says that this company has no paid employees in Québec) is the owner:
I Initiated contact with this company with a request for pricing in early April. After some back and forth I received a quote which was similar in price to other suppliers, decided to move forward with her because she offered a model that my boss liked. I was later informed that the model selected was discontinued, a different model was picked after she insisted on offering us models, I had already said we didn't want. In retrospect that should have been my first clue that this wasn't the right business for us.
In early May, I received a picture of a sample almost a full week after the date we were told we would receive it. She insisted that we had gotten it MONDAY even while we could look at the email stating clearly that it was received May 5th (a TUESDAY) at noon since emails are timestamped; the embroidery on the sample was rejected because it was entirely unacceptable (the biggest issue was that the lettering was really uneven).
I provided pictures of products we approved from other suppliers and clear indications of what we didn't like in her sample, thinking it would be no big deal. She flat out refused to make any change and disparaged the products we had approved of (which probably goes to show that we are absolutely not impossible to satisfy, you can also see that just in the last year I've left positive reviews for 2 other clothing companies). It's our (my boss') brand you would think we're allowed to have it look the way we want, but not according to her. On May 7th, I told her, by email, that if she didn't want to adjust the embroidery to be acceptable to us, we should agree on an amount for the sample and proceed with a cancellation. She wanted to ship us a bunch of hats that she had supposedly ordered for us which we refused. She then tried to go around me (her only contact so far) to go to the company's president. She tried to disparage me to the president calling me am intransigent young girl who was probably new at her job. Unfortunately for her, I've been with this company for years and my boss reiterated that if she didn't want to adjust the embroidery we wanted to be refunded. On May 14th he (my boss) sent a message demanding a refund. She then claimed that the situation was in the hands of "the authority".
The company I work for sent a formal notice (mise en demeure) in August.
On August 10 she claimed a cheque had been sent over a month ago, we never received anything. On September 28 she claimed a cheque had been mailed on the 25th, again we didn't get anything. Ultimately, an Interac transfer was received, on October 2nd, for 125$ less than we had given her. Personally, I don't think 125$ to produce a sample that was never physically sent to us is a reasonable price but if the boss wants to accept, I'm not going to argue. After making us wait 4 months and 18 days for a refund she has sent multiple emails DEMANDING that my boss forces me to take down my review. She wants me to remove my "annonce" (I think she means avis/review) within 48hrs. I'm not removing my review; I'm updating it to reflect the updated situation because I think people deserve to know what they're getting into.
A month ago the owner's response to my review was updated to include a threat of legal action, I have yet to receive a formal notice or to be contacted by a lawyer but she has reiterated her treats to my boss in an attempt to bully me into deleting my review. This account belongs to me personally.

Communication with this clinic is basically non-existent. They also don't apologize for not calling you back?? I feel like they missed every single social cues expected from a receptionist services. I've yet to have my tests done because it's been so difficult to book them, but based on the other reviews, I'm guessing it won't be a great experience either. Do yourself a favour and go elsewhere

Very Poor Service and Unprofessional Staff
I have had a very disappointing experience with this clinic. Whenever I book an appointment, I am often kept waiting for 1–2 hours, despite having a scheduled appointment time.
After my blood work, I was repeatedly told that someone would call me to provide my results, but I never received a call. The receptionist has also been extremely unprofessional and disrespectful. I have called multiple times, and instead of answering the phone, my calls were repeatedly disconnected or left hanging.
What frustrates me the most is that I recently missed an appointment and was charged a $150 no-show fee. I had actually called several times beforehand to cancel the appointment, but nobody answered my calls. Now I am being blamed for not showing up, even though I made multiple attempts to contact the clinic.
The staff used to be friendly, organized, and professional, but unfortunately, the service has changed significantly. The lack of communication, long waiting times, poor customer service, and attitude from the receptionist are extremely disappointing.
I am very frustrated with this clinic and would not recommend it to others. Please consider your options carefully before booking an appointment here.

I recently had a transvaginal ultrasound at this clinic, and it was by far the worst experience I have ever had.
The sonographer was extremely rough and unprofessional. I have had this procedure done before, so I know what to expect, but this was the most painful ultrasound I have ever experienced. Throughout the examination, she showed very little care or consideration for my comfort.

I arrived at the appointment with only mild abdominal discomfort, but after the ultrasound I developed severe abdominal pain.

My experience with the reception staff was just as disappointing. I was given a telephone follow-up appointment for the same week. I waited the entire morning for the call, unable to leave the house because I did not want to miss it. When no one called, I tried phoning the clinic repeatedly, but no one answered. I then emailed the clinic asking what had happened to my appointment, and was simply told that I had only an ultrasound and that my results had been sent to my family doctor—as if no follow-up appointment had ever existed.

I replied asking why no one had informed me that my appointment had been cancelled. I had waited all morning, anxious to discuss my results, and a simple phone call or email would have prevented all of this frustration. My email was never answered. Given the poor communication, I only hoped my results were actually sent to the correct physician.

I followed up with my doctor a week later, and she confirmed that they had never received my results. The Ultrasound clinic had told me that they sent my results directly to my doctor, which was not true.

I had to repeatedly chase the ultrasound clinic for my results, and eventually they sent it directly to me.

Overall, my experience at this clinic was extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
My Experience — Port Hope Location

If I could give zero stars, I would.

I am extremely disappointed and upset by my experience with this company’s Port Hope location.

This involves my daughter, who is a minor receiving mental-health therapy. She is a child who needs support, and as her parent, I trusted that she was in the care of a professional service that would communicate with us and treat our family fairly.

An appointment was apparently booked for my daughter without my knowledge or authorization. I was never notified that this appointment had been scheduled.

I only found out about it when I received an appointment reminder 24 hours before the scheduled appointment. I immediately contacted them to explain that I had not been aware of the appointment and that my daughter could not attend.

Despite this, I was charged a $165 cancellation fee because their policy requires 48 hours' notice.

How can a parent provide 48 hours' notice for an appointment they were never informed about and only discovered 24 hours beforehand?

To make matters worse, I was also charged for a therapy session that my daughter never attended. When I questioned the charge, I was told it was covered under their cancellation policy.

What makes this especially upsetting is that this is mental-health care for a child who is already in need of support. Families seeking therapy for their children are often already dealing with enough stress. We trusted this service and expected clear communication, transparency, and understanding.

Instead, this situation has added more stress and frustration to our family at a time when we were looking for support.

I am sharing this review because I don't want another parent to experience the same thing. If you have a child receiving therapy here, I strongly recommend making sure you are personally aware of every appointment scheduled and carefully reviewing any charges made to your card.

Parents seeking mental-health support for their children deserve to feel that they can trust the people and services involved in their child's care. This experience left us feeling very differently.

However, this person is far from an expert and her qualifications are questionable at best. She provided absolutely no value at all and simply collected a pay cheque. I would not recommend Chelsea Bodie, particularly for parents looking for counselling for their children.

My children saw Chelsea over a number of years, and I eventually became very concerned with the level of care, communication, and follow-up they received. I later learned through a formal complaint process that she had documented my son as having “deteriorated,” yet this was never communicated to me at the time and I saw no corresponding urgency or meaningful follow-up regarding that concern.

I was also extremely troubled by statements Chelsea made during the complaint process about interactions she allegedly had with me. In particular, it was stated that she offered follow-up appointments that I declined. I categorically dispute that this ever happened. Based on my experience, this has left me with serious concerns about the accuracy and reliability of her representations when her care was questioned.

Parents trust psychologists with incredibly important aspects of their children's wellbeing. I expect open communication, appropriate follow-up when a child's condition is deteriorating, and an accurate account of interactions with parents. Unfortunately, my experience left me without confidence in any of these areas.

I would not take my children back to Chelsea and would strongly encourage other parents to carefully consider their options before engaging her services.

They take your money and do nothing. Go to a real place like BDO. All these guys do is take your money than send you to a place like BDO that charges nothing.

I asked for a refund at the end since i had to solve the situation myself, which I now have and they played games about it until I gave up. They literally take your money for 3 months, let you credit get even more sewered and then send you to a real trustee.

Oh they also give you a $50 discount to review them positive, at the beginning when you know no better. Thats why they have so many decent reviews.

Those people doesn’t have license, they ‘re scammers, I took$4100 biweekly payments of $684 since July 2026, they ask me to stop paying my credits. I never missed the payments. i am in very situation now.

DO NOT USE! SAVE YOURSELF THE TIME AND MONEY!

I reached out to DS originally after seeing they offered Debt Consolidation services on their website. I knew I was not eligible for a consumer purposal as I had tried previously. In my calls with DS agent I expressed this and I was told that it is no problem they have programs for everyone in every situation.

After collecting all my debt documentation and sending it to them, I was informed I had to wait 45 business days before their “signing officer” could reach out to me, by law. During that time I had asked multiple times if my creditors were notified of my proceedings as I still wasn’t aware the type of program yet, and was assured they were.

Fast forward to the 45 business days mark, I still have not heard anything, creditors still calling and I still have no info to give them. I finally receive a call a week later from an Insolvency Trustee asking me if I’m in need of a consumer purposal.

The IT went through his process with me and after reviewing my documents that DS had sent him determined I was not able to qualify for a consumer purposal, which I had already known, the issue was a secured loan. As it carries 90% of my debt he recommended not proceeding any further. He also informed me that as he is governed under the Insolvency laws in Canada he has a 45 business day requirement to allow creditors to respond to the purposal. DebtSolvers has no such requirement. He also informed me that he randomly gets emails from them just saying “so and so needs a consumer purposal”. Save your time and money and go contact one directly if this is the route you want.

Also, the payments that DS guaranteed would not increase, was a lie, if I had been able to enroll in the CP the payments would have actually doubled.

Aswell with the payments I was making to DS over their waiting period I asked over and over to assurance that the money I was sending was going towards my debt/creditors, they assured me it was. After being dumped to an IT it clearly was not and I have no idea what has happened to the money I sent them.

Now, for the last two months I have been fighting over text, because my calls go unanswered, about getting a refund for the $2400+ I sent DebtSolvers over their “waiting” period. They continue to refuse the refund as they say there is other ways to finalize my file.

After this kind of lying and deception there is no way I will choose to continue business with Debt Solvers and anyone looks should save themselves the grief and hassle and reach out to an insolvency trustee themselves.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’d leave zero stars if I could.

My almost 70-year-old grandmother bought a Kia Soul from Sam. When she received the vehicle, it had absolutely no oil in the engine. It even came with half a jug of oil, which strongly suggests this was known before the sale.

Then, just two months later, while she was driving uphill in traffic, the rear wheel literally fell off. The wheel studs were found to be severely over-torqued and stretched, causing them to snap. The tires had previously been changed at this shop, so this should have been caught.

When my grandmother returned to have the issue corrected, their solution was to replace only the two studs that had snapped, while leaving the other damaged studs in place—and she was charged for it. They also failed to properly inspect the rotor, despite it having made direct contact with the asphalt when the wheel came off.

This is completely unacceptable. A nearly 70-year-old customer should not have to worry about whether a vehicle purchased from a dealership is properly maintained and safe to drive. The fact that these issues were either missed or ignored is extremely concerning.

On August 26, 2026, I had an extremely negative first-time shopping experience at ANC Tradings. My friend and I purchased several meat products, only to discover severe quality and labeling issues upon returning home:
1. Misidentified Meat & Overcharging: We selected two packages of frozen meat that appeared to be beef. The cashier agreed and charged us the beef rate of $5.99/lb (totaling $56.62 and $68.10). Once thawed, the meat was clearly pork—which retails locally for nearly half that price ($3.00–$3.30/lb). We were never informed the product was pork.
2. Inedible/Spoiled Product: A discounted package of chicken feet turned out to be severely freezer-burned and smelled/tasted spoiled after cooking, forcing us to throw it out.
On August 27, I emailed ANC Tradings Management with photos of our receipts and the meat, offering them a chance to resolve the issue directly. When they failed to reply, I called their office. The employee initially claimed she didn't get the email, so I resent it while on the line and verified receipt. She promised a follow-up call by the next day at the latest.
To date, ANC Tradings has completely ignored my attempts to reach them. Their willingness to sell mislabeled, spoiled products and then ghost paying customers shows a total lack of accountability. I strongly advise consumers to avoid this business.

one_star_reviews.text: This was one of the worst customer service experiences I have ever had and was extremely disappointing from start to finish. When I arrived, I had to wait about 10 minutes just to take my order because the clerk taking orders was outside smoking with friends instead of serving customers. I ordered my first beer, paid with my card, and even left an 18% tip, which came to about $12.63. Later, when I ordered my second beer, I was told that I had never paid for the first beer. I showed my bank statement as proof of payment, but the staff refused to acknowledge it and charged me for the first beer a second time. After I received my second beer, I went outside for a quick cigarette. I even left a napkin on my glass to indicate that I would be back. When I returned, my beer had been collected. When I asked what happened, I was simply told that they had taken it away because I had been out. At around 3:10am, I asked if they could replace the beer they had taken. I was told that they could no longer serve alcohol as it was past 3am. However, at the same time, I personally witnessed staff pouring alcoholic drinks for other customers and refusing to serve me. This inconsistency made the experience feel very unfair. This was my first visit and will definitely be my last. I experienced poor customer service, had to wait an unreasonable amount of time just to order, was charged twice despite showing proof of payment, had my drink taken away while I had been out for a short time and then refused to provide a replacement in a manner that seemed inconsistent with how they treated other customers. I left feeling disappointed, frustrated and completely unhappy with the way I was treated. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this place.

One star feels far too generous.

It has been 7–8 years since my mom, now in her 80s, switched to Dr. Dissanayake. Thankfully, we only need to see her once a year, because almost every visit has involved either a rescheduled appointment or a very long wait. We understand that doctors can be busy and that appointments can run over—we don’t mind waiting when patients are actually being seen.

Today, however, was particularly frustrating. We arrived before our scheduled appointment and checked in with the receptionist. We then waited more than 30 minutes past our appointment time while patients who arrived after us were called in to see other doctors and had already come and gone. During that same period, one doctor even called in three patients.

I eventually went to the receptionist to ask how much longer we would have to wait. She then told me she would “let the doctor know that you are here,” which meant that, apparently, our check-in had not even been communicated to the doctor. We had been waiting all that time for nothing.

Within a minute, the doctor came out casually, without any apology or acknowledgment of the delay. I did express my frustration because patients’ time is valuable too, and there should be some basic consideration for that.

At the end, she simply suggested that we could switch to another doctor.

After 7–8 years, I would expect much better communication, organization, and respect for patients’ time. Unfortunately, today’s experience was extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would like to share my experience with the academy's Caledon program. While the coach is highly skilled and knowledgeable, there were several concerns regarding scheduling, communication, and overall service delivery.

The coach appears to be managing training across multiple GTA locations while also organizing and playing matches. As a result, the Caledon program often seemed to receive lower priority. On a few occasions, sessions were cancelled due to weather forecasts even when little or no rain occurred near the training ground. Despite advance notice of improved conditions, the coach was unavailable to attend, suggesting other commitments took precedence.

During weekday matches with older or more advanced players, the coach's reactions to mistakes such as wides, poor shots, misfields, or dropped catches sometimes felt overly critical rather than constructive, which can be discouraging for young players.

At registration, families were given options for Saturday-only, Sunday-only, or both weekend days. Later, the two-day option was removed and everyone was shifted to Sundays, including those who had specifically preferred Saturdays.

Sunday sessions were originally communicated as 8:30 AM to 11:00 AM, but start times frequently changed to 9:30 AM based on the coach's other commitments. During hot summer months, earlier sessions would have been more suitable for young children, yet Caledon participants were expected to accommodate schedule changes.

The academy advertised 2.5-hour sessions; however, about 15 minutes were often spent setting up equipment and sessions commonly ended 15 minutes early, reducing actual training time to roughly 2 hours.

When a session was missed due to the coach being ill, parents were informed of a makeup session the following Saturday. However, late Friday night, parents were asked via WhatsApp to confirm attendance, with a minimum of six children required. Some families responded positively, but the session was cancelled due to "insufficient numbers." This approach seemed unreasonable given the short notice, the fact that not all parents actively monitor WhatsApp, and that attendance could reasonably have been assumed unless parents explicitly declined.

The following weekend, a Saturday session was missed despite minimal rainfall, and Sunday's session was cancelled due to rain, resulting in two missed sessions. To compensate, the academy offered a Tuesday session from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM and called it a "bonus" session. In reality, it was a makeup session, 30 minutes shorter than the regular program and held during shorter daylight hours.

While I appreciate the coach's cricketing expertise, inconsistent scheduling, communication issues, reduced training time, and the perception that the Caledon program was given lower priority affected the overall experience. I eventually requested and received a partial refund, although the response left the impression that constructive feedback was not particularly welcomed because only few other parents had raised similar concerns publicly.

I share this feedback in the hope that it helps improve the experience for future participants.

We’ve given this D Spot location two chances because we believe in second chances… apparently more than they believe in serving food on time. 😂

The first visit: we waited over 30 minutes for our order. Meanwhile, people who ordered after us were getting their food first.

We thought that maybe it was just a bad day, so we came back a second time and this time, we ordered a milk cake. Surely dessert couldn’t take that long, right?

Wrong...

Over an hour later, our milk cake finally arrived. At that point, I had emotionally moved on from the dessert. And unfortunately, the cake itself was pretty underwhelming for the amount of time we waited.

And once again, people who walked in about 10 minutes after us got their orders before we did.

The service is basically self serve, you order your food yourself at the counter and pick it up yourself so I’m still trying to figure out where the hour long wait comes from...

(Likely an understaffed kitchen... if the kitchen is understaffed, that would at least explain the wait times but if that’s the case, this should have been addressed a long time ago, especially considering we gave the location months before coming back for our second visit.)

As well as the cleanliness didn’t exactly help the experience either. The floors had chocolate all over them, and our table didn’t appear to be getting cleaned either. We’re here for dessert, not to participate in an archaeological digging. 😂)

I’ve been to other D Spot locations and had much better experiences, so unfortunately this location just isn’t it.

Two visits, two long waits, two disappointments. We gave it a fair chance. At this point, the only thing we’ll be ordering is a reservation at a different D-Spot. 😕

I’m usually pretty easygoing with restaurants, as my other reviews show. But if I don’t say anything, the next person might order dessert and end up spending the rest of their evening here.

⭐️ Extremely Unprofessional
I never leave bad reviews, but this was honestly one of the worst spa experiences I’ve had.

Update: Even the response was unprofessional. Your website clearly advertised a hair treatment with a professional blow-dry, but my hair was not completely dried or light styled, so I had to finish styling it myself afterward. A blow-dry should include light styling, not simply drying the hair with a hair dryer using one hand.

The process was also not fully completed either, as my scalp was not checked afterward. But wanna charge $20 extra after I spent $142 on this kind of service.

I also found the comment about me taking time with my makeup completely inaccurate—I did not redo any makeup. I came in carrying only a small purse and simply used your washroom after styling my hair. 😅

The head spa itself was okay, but the service afterward was extremely unprofessional. The website advertises a blow-dry, yet the staff member simply used a hair dryer with no brush, no comb, and no styling whatsoever. She even left parts of my hair wet, saying that drying it completely would make mire frizzy. All she use is a dryer and her hand to dry my hair ofcourse the hair get frizzy. I was then told I had to style my own hair using their styling brush while she sat and waited for her next client.

A blow-dry obviously includes properly drying the hair with at least basic/light styling. If your staff don’t understand what a blow-dry includes, it shouldn’t be advertised on your website or said professional blow dry.

She was also rushing me because another client was arriving in 10 minutes, so I had to finish styling my own hair while being pressured to leave. There was no final scalp check after the exfoliation either.

To make matters worse, I was asked to pay additional because my treatment was taking longer than expected and she had to use extra product. At one point, when I was trying to get her attention, she told me to “stop screaming.” Yes, she specifically used the word “screaming,” which I found completely unnecessary and extremely disrespectful.
I paid for a service and ended up having to finish it myself. Unprofessional, rushed, and absolutely not worth the price. I would not recommend this place

I am not typically someone who leaves reviews or jumps from club to club, but I felt a strong responsibility to share our experience so other families don't make the same mistake.
The practising conditions here are unacceptable. For a 7v7 , they have 15 children onto a roster in a space that isn't even large enough for 7 players to practis properly. Despite this, management insists there is 'plenty of room.' Since looking for a new club, I’ve realized that no other academy in the area charges this much for such poor conditions. For the same price, you can find longer sessions, better facilities, and coaches with proven results. And if you will more games, and better competition you have an option to put your child to play stronger leagues.
Furthermore, you are forced to pay $400 annually for a gear package; if you don't buy it, your child is barred from playing in games. Most alarmingly, when we tried to leave on a nice way,we were met with threats. They threatened that if we don't pay for the next season (in which my child will not participate) that they will put a record in his name in Ontario soccer and he won’t be allowed to play soccer in other clubs.
There is much more to write, but I think this is enough
This is not how an academy should be run.

The club offers an experience for the players that looks great on paper but fails to follow through. The management is poor and clearly dont care what happens with the teams. It became very clear this returning year.

We decided to give them one more shot and regret even signing up for the  2025/26. The coaching of the GU14 team was pitiful, Brielle was clearly not qualified to coach. There was zero transparency and practice/training had no intensity. Coach spent most of her time on her phone instead of having training sessions organized and ready. The indoor and most of the outdoor season went on with terrible training and match results

These problems were addressed to the club by multiple parents and nothing was done to take care of the issues until very late in the season.

It wasnt until the end of the season the club finally fired Brielle and replaced her with a new coach. The new coach managed to recover some of the season, but unfortunately she was thrown into a fire and had her work cut out. She was the only good thing to happen to the girls.

If you are looking to join the force, I would recommend reaching out to parents and pass members/coaches of the club. It is a heavy price to pay ($4200+ and $400+ for kit) for mediocre results

Oh Matt, you're such a shill. It certainly gives the impression that this post is coming from someone with close connections to the club. (admins wife) The truth is, if you're showing an interest in joining Force, you may be promised the world. However, once your registration and payment are made, some parents may find that level off communication, support, and follow through doesn't match what was initially presented. If you're thinking about joining Force, I'd encourage you to do your own research and ask some important questions. Why are so many players and coaches now leaving? Talk to current and former parents, players, and coaches. Ask about their experiences before making your decision. Don't rely solely on what you're told during recruitment process.

Then, we (the four children) left messages and waited for months. When I called and demanded a return call, I spoke to an assistant. I was given a phone appointment with Lucas Chicoine-Ouelette. During the call, Mr. Chicoine-Ouelette began the conversation with disparaging remarks about my deceased father. He spoke to me as casually as if chatting with a friend, without any professionalism.
During this brief conversation, I agreed to handle the will. I asked questions and inquired if he could guide me through the process. He said he would call me back; he had to check something first. More than three weeks passed without any news. My brothers, sister, and I decided to no longer do business with Lucas Chicoine-Ouelette. I called and left a message saying we no longer needed his services. We contacted another notary. Then, suddenly, my sister was informed that Maître Lucas Chicoine-Ouelette had filed a complaint against the four "detestable" children. A judge then appointed someone else as executor of the will. Fortunately, this person was very kind to us. A story with a happy ending.

P.S. Maître Lucas Chicoine-Ouelette, please know that you did me a favor by filing your complaint.

It’s unfortunate, as I contacted RES-Q-DRAIN specifically because of their excellent reviews.

I reached out regarding corrective plumbing work following a significant home insurance claim and provided an inspection report prepared by an engineering firm.

I was told they would come on Monday, but no one showed up, and I had to follow up myself to get an update.

During the call that followed, I completely understand that an in-person visit is necessary before preparing a quote. However, I was told that the inspection report was not of interest and that I should not tell him what to do. When I explained that our insurance company would require a written quote following the visit, I was repeatedly interrupted and eventually told that I was “talking too much.”

When someone is dealing with an urgent situation following a major loss, basic respect, communication, and professionalism should be the bare minimum like especially for a company working in this field.

Unfortunately, we decided not to proceed with their services.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would like to share my experience with the academy's Caledon program. While the coach is highly skilled and knowledgeable, there were several concerns regarding scheduling, communication, and overall service delivery.

The coach appears to be managing training across multiple GTA locations while also organizing and playing matches. As a result, the Caledon program often seemed to receive lower priority. On a few occasions, sessions were cancelled due to weather forecasts even when little or no rain occurred near the training ground. Despite advance notice of improved conditions, the coach was unavailable to attend, suggesting other commitments took precedence.

During weekday matches with older or more advanced players, the coach's reactions to mistakes such as wides, poor shots, misfields, or dropped catches sometimes felt overly critical rather than constructive, which can be discouraging for young players.

At registration, families were given options for Saturday-only, Sunday-only, or both weekend days. Later, the two-day option was removed and everyone was shifted to Sundays, including those who had specifically preferred Saturdays.

Sunday sessions were originally communicated as 8:30 AM to 11:00 AM, but start times frequently changed to 9:30 AM based on the coach's other commitments. During hot summer months, earlier sessions would have been more suitable for young children, yet Caledon participants were expected to accommodate schedule changes.

The academy advertised 2.5-hour sessions; however, about 15 minutes were often spent setting up equipment and sessions commonly ended 15 minutes early, reducing actual training time to roughly 2 hours.

When a session was missed due to the coach being ill, parents were informed of a makeup session the following Saturday. However, late Friday night, parents were asked via WhatsApp to confirm attendance, with a minimum of six children required. Some families responded positively, but the session was cancelled due to "insufficient numbers." This approach seemed unreasonable given the short notice, the fact that not all parents actively monitor WhatsApp, and that attendance could reasonably have been assumed unless parents explicitly declined.

The following weekend, a Saturday session was missed despite minimal rainfall, and Sunday's session was cancelled due to rain, resulting in two missed sessions. To compensate, the academy offered a Tuesday session from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM and called it a "bonus" session. In reality, it was a makeup session, 30 minutes shorter than the regular program and held during shorter daylight hours.

While I appreciate the coach's cricketing expertise, inconsistent scheduling, communication issues, reduced training time, and the perception that the Caledon program was given lower priority affected the overall experience. I eventually requested and received a partial refund, although the response left the impression that constructive feedback was not particularly welcomed because only few other parents had raised similar concerns publicly.

I share this feedback in the hope that it helps improve the experience for future participants.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing and concerning experience.

We ordered food from Delhi Boyz and noticed what appeared to be mould on the bread/bun after we had already started eating. We also found buns in the restaurant with a date label that raised concerns about whether they were still within their proper use period. I have photos from our visit showing both the bread and the packaging/date label. What made the experience worse was how the situation was handled. When we brought the issue to the worker’s attention, instead of acknowledging our concern and checking the product properly, he argued with us and insisted that the buns were not expired. Regardless of the explanation about the date, visible mould or questionable bread should be taken seriously, especially by a restaurant serving food to the public.
Mistakes can happen, but food safety concerns should be handled professionally—with an apology, an immediate check of the remaining stock, and appropriate corrective action—not an argument with the customer.

This experience seriously affected our confidence in the restaurant’s food handling and quality-control practices. I hope management reviews what happened, checks their bread inventory and storage procedures, and trains staff on how to respond appropriately when customers raise legitimate food-safety concerns.

I would not recommend eating here based on this experience.

I boarded here 2 years ago. Now that I’m safe I feel like I can share my experience here.
This was the first stop on my boarding adventures.

Long story short, the wife was interested in the horse I recently purchased and thought if I boarded with them she could take him from me.
They tried teaching my horse that the “ wife “ was his mom and even in front of me by accident.
The wife told me I could get my boys feet done when her horse did as hers had to be sleep sedated. That horse mysteriously died one day. And no longer could my horse get his feet done lol

The husband is a police officer who attempted to confine me in their barn after expressing that their hay made my horse sick and I didn’t not want it in his stall. Everytime I took a step the husband took a step blocking me from exiting the barn. After saying I am recording this conversation I was told I had 20 minutes with my horse and they were calling the police to have me removed from the property.
Now the wife luckily told me her husband is a police officer so police threatening me to call the police on me? I knew right away I had the upper hand and called them as soon as I was free from the barn
I was recording the whole thing bc I had a feeling something was off that day. Thank god I did.
The Sargent had to come out. The husband would not leave me alone and kept approaching me while on the phone with 911.
The only thing that saved me in this situation was the fact I never stopped recording the incident which lasted over an hour.

This is not a safe environment and I would not recommend anyone board here if they value their life and their horses life.

Yes it’s 2 years later, my boy and I are not in a facility we have our own farm now.

I’m sharing my story in hopes this never happens to anyone ever again.

Thank you 🙏 god is amazing.

Extremely disappointing and unprofessional experience with Aaron’s Property Management.

We returned the unit and all keys on August 17. At the time of the handover, a member of their management team inspected the unit with us present, and the signed move-out documentation recorded the condition of the apartment and confirmed that the appliances were working.

Despite this, management later raised a cleaning charge, which we repeatedly disputed in writing, and subsequently raised a separate washing machine issue after the new tenant had already taken possession.

We clearly communicated our position, provided supporting documentation, disputed the charges, and expressly stated that we did not agree to any deduction from our $500 key deposit.

Our final email was not answered. Instead, we received a payment of $262.70, with the disputed $237.30 cleaning charge deducted from our deposit, without any further response addressing our objection.

We find the way this was handled extremely disappointing. A disputed charge should at the very least be addressed through clear and professional communication, particularly when the unit had already been inspected at handover and its condition documented by their own representative. Making the deduction without responding to our final objection showed a serious lack of communication and professionalism.

Based on our experience with the handling of our move-out and deposit, we would not recommend Aaron’s Property Management.

⚠️ Be very careful when renting a property managed by this company.

Our experience was extremely disappointing, and I would specifically like to mention Tony, who was in charge of handling our case.

After we moved out, the apartment was inspected by a representative of the company, who confirmed that the unit was clean and in good condition. We also have photos and documentation supporting the condition of the apartment at move-out.

Despite this, Tony authorized a cleaning charge against our deposit without our authorization, even though the apartment had already been inspected and the cleaning had been confirmed as satisfactory.

From our experience, this was not a fair or professional way to handle a move-out. We believe tenants should carefully document the condition of their property, take photos, and obtain written confirmation during the move-out process.

I am sharing this review so other tenants are aware of our experience, particularly when dealing with Tony and the move-out process. We expected transparency and professionalism, but unfortunately, that was not our experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
I contacted Samsung Support because my Samsung gas stove was producing yellow flames. Before calling for service, I had already cleaned the burner heads and caps thoroughly, but the issue continued. Samsung provided me with the contact information for Core Appliances, so I arranged a service visit.

Eduardo from Core Appliances came to my home to inspect the stove. Unfortunately, I was very disappointed with the service. There seemed to be very little actual diagnosis or troubleshooting performed. After looking at the stove, he simply suggested replacing the burners, which he said would cost approximately $130 each, in addition to a $150 service fee.

He also mentioned that the burners "didn't look correct." I am not sure what he meant by that, as these are the original Samsung burner heads that came with the stove when I purchased it approximately two years ago. They have never been replaced or modified.

I specifically asked how he could determine that the burner heads were the problem without performing any proper diagnostic testing. His response was essentially that he was "pretty sure" the burners were the issue and that I should order and replace them first. If replacing them did not solve the problem, he would then come back to investigate the internal components.

I find this approach very concerning. The purpose of paying a professional service fee is to properly diagnose the issue before recommending potentially expensive replacement parts. Asking a customer to spend hundreds of dollars replacing original parts based on an assumption, and only investigating further if that doesn't work, does not feel like professional appliance service.

I expected a qualified technician to troubleshoot the actual cause of the yellow flames and determine whether the issue was related to the burner heads, gas/air mixture, regulator, or another component before recommending replacement parts.

Unfortunately, that was not my experience, and I was left without a clear diagnosis or solution despite paying for a professional service visit.

According to the company’s website, the property is advertised as having full-time security and a fully functional CCTV surveillance system. As a resident of the building, I would like to highlight the following discrepancies and issues:
1- Security Presence: Security is not provided on a daily basis. There is only a guard on duty once or twice a week for an 8-hour shift.
2- CCTV System & Theft Incidents: On two separate occasions, my locked bicycle was stolen from the designated bicycle parking area. Although I reported both incidents to the police, building management was unable to provide any CCTV footage due to a significant number of non-functioning cameras, leaving my financial losses unrecovered.
3- Main Entrance Door Accessibility: The main entrance door is manual rather than automated. Due to its heavy weight and size, elderly residents, individuals with disabilities, and young children are unable to open it, rendering the entrance inaccessible for them.
4- Parking & Trash Room Access: The entrance to the parking area and the trash room are shared, and unfortunately, the connecting staircase lacks an accessible ramp for elderly and disabled residents.
5- Laundry Room Accessibility: The entryway to the laundry room consists of four steep steps and lacks an accessible ramp for elderly residents and individuals with disabilities.

I then received another email that if I did not pay the $200 before a final date that they would send a collection agency to receive the funds. I asked again in that email what the charge was for and was not given an explanation.

I ended up paying it so that this matter would be done with, but I was really unimpressed with how Deeks handled their business and would not recommend them as they are run now.

one_star_reviews.text:
The Large Cash Deposit: The contractor demands a very substantial dollars upfront for deposit and "materials" and then disappears

I am sharing my experience with Sovereign Power Corp. because I believe prospective homeowners should carefully consider the risks before making a substantial payment for a solar installation.
I signed a contract with Sovereign Power Corp. on June 17, 2026, for the supply and installation of a solar panel system. I paid a very substantial dollar upfront, representing 90% of the contract price.
The installation was initially expected to take place in mid-July 2026. That deadline passed, and the supply and installation have continued to be delayed. I have been given various explanations for the delays, but the project remains un-started.
What has been particularly concerning to me is the limited communication and lack of clear progress information despite repeated follow-ups. Given the substantial amount of money already paid, I expected much more timely communication and a clear plan for completing the contracted work.
As of the date of this review, I do not have supply or installation of the solar installation that I contracted and paid for.
I am not making any allegation about the company's intentions. I am simply documenting my own experience and encouraging other homeowners to do thorough due diligence before making a large upfront payment. I recommend carefully reviewing the payment terms, installation commitments, cancellation/refund provisions, company history, references, and available consumer information before signing a contract.
I hope Sovereign Power Corp. resolves my situation promptly and fulfills its contractual commitments.
Price assessment
Overpriced

Do not support spaces that subject independent artists to corporate blacklists. Take your business elsewhere.

I was on the opposing side of a civil dispute where Mr. Dobre represented the other party. As a self-represented party in this negotiation, that experience felt one-sided from the start. All I can say is be very careful when dealing with a person like him. I also ordered a tabouli salad separately. The gentleman in the blue shirt said he would check, then came back and said it was no longer on the menu. Even though it was clearly listed on the menu screen.

When I asked for extra salad on the side, he told me they had no extra containers. I pointed out the containers that were clearly displayed right in front of me, and he then changed his response to, “No, we don’t do that.” I was even willing to pay extra.

The whole interaction felt like one excuse after another instead of simply being upfront about what they could or couldn’t provide.

On top of that, the meat was dry, and the garlic sauce barely tasted like garlic. The consistency and taste were almost closer to mayonnaise. Very buttery and oily rather than garlicky.

Overall, both the customer service and food quality have declined. Very disappointing experience.

We asked why is a north carolina ribber there and he isn't.... he told us some wild story about the lions club not allowing him to be part of the ribfest.

So the local ribfest don't let indigenous locals participate.

So basically... out of town ribbers come here to gouge tourists who come here to spend their tax dollars in the community... only for the ribbers to take all their money down to London and to North Carolina.

Next year, the only place to go for Ribs is Sheg Pow Wow.

one_star_reviews.text:
I took my friend, who’s visiting Ottawa, to this place hoping we’d have a nice breakfast together, but unfortunately, the experience was disappointing from start to finish.

We sat down for 20 minutes before a waitress even acknowledged us. I eventually had to wave her down just to get someone to come take our order. Twenty minutes is honestly insane; I’ve never experienced anything like that at a breakfast restaurant. And it wasn’t just our waitress either; the staff seemed to constantly walk past tables without looking at or acknowledging customers.

The food took another 10 minutes or so to arrive, but unfortunately, it wasn’t anything special. The bacon was dry, the eggs were bland, and overall, the food was lacking in flavour. The French roast was probably the only thing that wasn’t bad.

Once we finished eating, we waited another 15 minutes and no one came to check on us or clear the table. Again, I had to wave at a waitress. Not even call her over, literally just wave, to get her attention. The waitress was a tall, slim redhead with a tattoo on the inside of her forearm. She clearly did not appreciate me waving her over and proceeded to give me a terrible stare, even as we were leaving.

Honestly, probably one of the worst breakfast experiences I’ve had. And it’s especially disappointing because I brought my friend there while she’s visiting Ottawa. This is definitely not the kind of experience you want someone to have when they’re discovering the city for the first time.
